extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), installation commanders, CE publication editors, contracting officers, Staff Judge Advocates (SJAs), and OCPA staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for Army public affairs publications, civilian-enterprise (CE) newspapers, awards submissions, Privacy Act release decisions, and clearance of contractor-originated materials. Includes editorial policies, advertising/ sponsorship rules, award/competition criteria, feasibility study steps for CE newspapers, and release/clearance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline usage and rank styling
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may use bylines over stories. Using rank is optional but will be consistent in style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentioning commercially sponsored AFE and MWR events
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercially sponsored Armed Forces Entertainment and MWR events may be mentioned with other pertinent facts in news stories and announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event titles using the name of commercial sponsors may be included if newsworthy and if the use clearly meets Army needs. See AR 215–1 for policy governing commercial sponsorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment reviews without implied endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Book, radio, television, movie, restaurant, and other entertainment reviews may be included if there is no implication of DA selective benefit or endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting gratuities in connection with these reviews is prohibited by DoD 5500.07–R. This paragraph does not prevent PA staff members from accepting press credentials or passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal treatment for approved private organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: All private organizations approved to operate on the installation may have meetings announced and other material considered for use; no organization will receive preferential treatment, including authorized veteran organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to the editor editorial control
rubrics_metrics.description: CE and AF publication editors will edit letters to the editor at their discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands are not obligated to respond to or return unsolicited editorial material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on covering ongoing test/evaluation programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Covering ongoing test or evaluation programs is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions to policy are through channels to OCPA (see para 6–6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial advertising identification
rubrics_metrics.description: All commercial advertising should be clearly identified, including advertising supplements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paid advertorials and advertising supplements may be included but must be clearly labeled as advertising and readily distinguishable from editorial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website linking to commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: DA websites are normally discouraged from linking to commercial activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commander may authorize an installation’s website to be linked to the website carrying the authorized CE publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: No implication of Army commercial endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications and websites will not contain any material implying Army endorsement of a commercial product, commodity, or service.

rubrics_metrics.name: No subscription to primarily-advertising services
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications and websites will not subscribe, even at no cost, to a commercial or feature wire or other service whose primary purpose is advertising or promoting commercial products, commodities, or services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisements must comply with equal opportunity policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications and websites will not carry any advertisement that violates or rejects DA equal opportunity policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public service awards coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders at all levels may recognize private citizens, local community leaders, and citizen groups and organizations for their support of the Army by public service awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders will coordinate recommendations with the local civilian personnel office, which normally controls the supply of awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries for Community Relations Award eligibility and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries to be considered eligible for judging must be submitted through command channels to OCPA by released deadline dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should cover planning, execution, and results, and contain a summary of not more than two single-spaced, typed pages describing the program or event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for national award submissions (Silver Anvil)
rubrics_metrics.description: National recognition (Silver Anvil) may be achieved through external competitions; OCPA issues guidance for preparing entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award encourages improved performance and program techniques. Competition is open; PRSA membership is not required and will not affect judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: MG Keith L. Ware competition entry standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must meet the highest standards of production, presentation, execution, professional excellence, and originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An HQDA letter to ACOM PAOs announces specific rules and categories for the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-specific eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual awards recognize specific types of excellence (e.g., Soldier-writer, civilian writer, new military writer, videographer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges consider the applicable award’s purpose (storytelling, journalism, videography) and eligibility (e.g., enlisted Soldiers with less than 24 months for 'new' awards); awards are often named in honor of individuals to reflect the intended quality or career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army PA Hall of Fame nomination eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees must meet eligibility criteria: retired at least 3 years from active federal service, with exceptions for departure other than retirement; deceased nominees are not bound by the 3-year rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those who did not retire must have served a minimum of 7 years in a superior manner or have made significant and lasting contributions to the community or Army PA career field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hall of Fame selection limits and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPA chairs an annual review panel and sets a maximum limit of three nominees as recommended by the panel for induction into the Hall of Fame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An OCPA letter of instruction establishes detailed guidelines and procedures for nomination and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility study objective for CE newspapers
rubrics_metrics.description: The study’s objectives are to develop a list of qualified companies potentially interested in competing for a contract to print a CE newspaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs should use local standard installation or division personnel office data; commanders are not required to produce CE newspapers but should use digital platforms to engage audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with contracting office and SJA for CE feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin feasibility studies by coordinating with the local contracting office and SJA and brief the contracting office on the provisions of this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite the contracting representative to appointments with printers and assure them printers will be informed that a contract or agreement is not being sought at this time; contracting office should attend meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicizing potential CE newspaper contract
rubrics_metrics.description: To publicize the potential CE newspaper contract to commercial sources, the contracting officer should announce it in the Commerce Business Daily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where additional publicity is necessary, use press releases or advertisements in local area newspapers to develop commercial interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing contents for potential printers (mission and audience fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a briefing that sells the CE concept: include a brief mission statement of the community or unit and the newspaper, explaining how the newspaper meets the interests and needs of the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market demographics to include in CE briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed demographics: military population broken into junior enlisted, senior enlisted, and officers (include RC and retirees); civilian population; total military payroll; total civilian payroll; grade demographics with ranges; number of children; local national employees/payroll; number of family members; geographical dispersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide round figures; do not attempt to calculate taxes or allowances; list monthly pay for grade categories where applicable; if data available from local schools, include number of children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on purchasing power and captive market
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize purchasing power and that the paper reaches a captive market with exclusive distribution access to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include other market facts (where people shop, work, live, relax) and a resource study to define demographics and buying potentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying potential printers
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify potential printers through local chambers of commerce, business directories, and the local contracting office; check local publications for printer names and addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check post exchange, commissary, library, and clubs for newspapers or guides distributed in area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred contact method with printers
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact printing representatives to indicate interest in meeting to discuss producing the newspaper; face-to-face contact is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scheduling attempts are unsuccessful, forward documentation through PAO channels to the ACOM PAO with dates, times, and descriptions; authorized funds may be used for printing Army newspapers only after it is documented that a CE newspaper is not feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducting meetings with printing representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin meetings by informing the representative that the objective is information gathering and not obtaining an agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that specifications and official contacts, if they come, will be handled by the contracting office; do not imply a contract during informational meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation content and honesty with printers
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the representative the newspaper, obtain CE newspapers from other installations, explain differences, present demographics, and show profit potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful not to mislead (e.g., do not present press run as readership); discuss distribution potential and official distribution channels; obtain case study information from other printers serving military installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding information flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform interested representatives that their contact information and that of other prospective bidders will be provided to the contracting office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting for CE requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands will follow the provisions of this regulation for CE contracting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add realistic provisions so long as they do not contradict the regulation. A successful civilian printer the first year may allow negotiation of additional specifications and improved services the second year. The contracting office and the SJA are key executors in negotiating contracts and changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the Privacy Act for release decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'individual' in the Privacy Act applies only to living U.S. citizens or aliens admitted for permanent residence; minors/incompetents may exercise rights via parent/legal guardian; Privacy Act confers no rights on deceased persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information in a Privacy Act system of records may be exempt from release under FOIA. Under FOIA exemption six, privacy interests of a deceased person’s surviving family members are considered; withhold to protect their peace of mind (examples include autopsy reports and graphic details of murder). See AR 25–55 for full FOIA exemptions list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age/date-of-birth releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: Age or date of birth is not routinely or normally releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for disclosure must be evaluated and balanced against the degree of personal privacy invasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home of record and present address releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: No general rule exists; requests are weighted case-by-case. Home of record may usually be released if no street address is given; present location (e.g., city) may be provided but not street address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the desires of the individual or next of kin; consent removes the problem, but their desires do not necessarily control the decision because FOIA balancing may still require disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marital status releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual’s marital status is not routinely or normally disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for disclosure must be evaluated and balanced against the degree of personal invasion of privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards, decorations, and citations releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: Award, decoration, or citation information is releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information is usually publicized in the installation newspaper and there is often a visible token to be worn on the uniform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/schooling/specialty releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on major area of study, school, year of graduation, degree, and specialty designator is generally releasable under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, information about an individual’s race is not releasable because its release may constitute an unwarranted privacy invasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Race may be released when relevant to the essential facts (e.g., racially oriented protest or altercation) or when it is relevant to the essential facts of a case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of discharge releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative discharge character is not releasable; discharges resulting from punitive (court-martial) proceedings are releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court-martial proceedings are public; the approved sentence and subsequent clemency actions, if any, are releasable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty status releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: Duty status information is releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible releases include information about unauthorized absence or desertion, hospitalization, when a Servicemember is in civil authorities’ custody awaiting trial, or confinement awaiting trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel board decisions releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of personnel boards are releasable after decision by final approving authority if the board action applies to a category of persons; otherwise they are not releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results affecting groups (promotion boards, augmentation boards) are releasable. Results of individual-impact boards (administrative discharge boards, aviator flight boards) are not generally releasable. Information that has become public through the individual or counsel may be confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph releasability
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs in DoD custody taken for official purposes are generally releasable unless they depict matters that would constitute a clearly unwarranted personal privacy invasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award ceremony photos, official selection file photos, chain-of-command photos, and similar photos are generally releasable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names/duty addresses for sensitive units
rubrics_metrics.description: The name and duty address of a member assigned to a unit that is sensitive, routinely deployable, or stationed in a foreign territory is not routinely releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosing such information may pose a security threat. The releasing authority (normally the Soldier’s unit commander) must weigh public interest against invasion of personal privacy. ATSD(PA) is the sole approving authority for releasing rosters that list members of this type of unit by name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected health information (PHI) release rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Protected health information will not be released without the prior consent of the individual or the individual’s representative if incapacitated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical unit commanders are the release authority for their commands. Consent will be recorded on DA Form 4876.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor-originated materials clearance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: In prescribing procedures for submission, review, and clearance of industry-originated information materials, the DA defers to Army and industry interface guidance in the FAR, AFARS, and DFARS and the contract terms when a contract exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements apply to educational institutions receiving information from any Army element on pre-award negotiations, contract awards, letter contracts, modifications, or grants to carry out military R&D projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on releasing procurement information without approval
rubrics_metrics.description: DA agencies and contractors will not release procurement information on Army-contracted research and development projects without prior approval and clearance from the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Acquisition, Logistics and Technology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified contract handling and security criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A classified contract requires access to classified information to submit a bid/proposal or to perform the contract; a contract may be classified though the document itself is not classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a classified contract exists, the contractor is guided by security items in the contract and by the terms of the security agreement. Security criteria are shown on DD Form 254. DoDM 5220.22, Volume 2; DoD 5220.22–M; and AR 380–49 contain procedures to safeguard classified defense information and procedures for proposed release of information which contractors, subcontractors, vendors, or suppliers will have access to or possess.
